response.consequence: After a successful update or any refetch that returns new data, the event type editor is torn down and rebuilt. Form state, the current tab and focus are lost, the editor flashes blank, and the `ref` handle and `onFormStateChange` are briefly detached. Embedding apps that call `validateForm` or `handleFormSubmit` through the ref can hit a null ref during the reset.
response.explanation: The change adds `eventTypeQueryData` to the dependency array of the effect whose cleanup calls `invalidateQueries` and `resetQueries`. The comment on that cleanup says it should run only on unmount or when the event type id changes. Now the cleanup also runs each time the query data reference changes, for example after a save invalidates and refetches the query. At that point the cleanup resets the query, so `data` becomes undefined. `if (!eventTypeQueryData) return null;` then unmounts the whole `EventType` form, and it remounts when the refetch finishes.
response.title: Effect cleanup now resets the event-type query whenever its data changes, not only on unmount or id change

response.consequence: After a booking is reassigned, routing-form insights show the wrong host name, email and avatar for that booking. The data is silently inconsistent, and the only fix is a backfill.
response.explanation: The booking update trigger fires on a change to "userId" (line 258). Its SET list (lines 195-211) writes "bookingUserId" = NEW."userId" but never updates "bookingUserName", "bookingUserEmail" or "bookingUserAvatarUrl". refresh_routing_form_response_denormalized fills those three columns from users (lines 66-68). The user trigger only fires on changes to the users table, so it does not repair them. When a booking is reassigned to another user, the denormalized row therefore has the new bookingUserId but still carries the old user's name, email and avatar. The row stays wrong until that user's profile happens to change or someone runs a backfill. The reported insert-order concern is likely not a defect. The response UPDATE trigger (lines 122-125) re-runs the full refresh when routedToBookingUid is set after the booking exists, and that refresh does populate these columns. I did not check application code for the order of the response and booking writes.
response.title: Booking trigger updates bookingUserId but leaves bookingUserName, bookingUserEmail and bookingUserAvatarUrl stale

response.consequence: On Linux, rerunning the script leaves a stale webhook URL in .env while reporting success. Wrappers or CI that check the exit code cannot see tunnel startup failures.
response.explanation: The script updates an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with `sed -i '' -E ...`. That form only works with BSD/macOS sed. GNU sed on Linux treats `''` as an input file name, so the command fails and the .env file is not updated. The script then still prints the "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL" message. Separately, `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`. The failure paths (rate limit hit, no tunnel URL extracted) call `cleanup`, so the script reports success when it failed.
response.title: Webhook test script's `sed -i ''` is macOS-only and failures exit with status 0

hypotheses.failure_mode: The booking insert/update trigger refreshes denormalized rows with WHERE rfrd."bookingId" = NEW.id. If a form response is inserted before its booking exists, or if routedToBookingUid is set later, the denormalized row has a NULL bookingId. The booking trigger then matches nothing, so the row keeps NULL booking, status, and UTM fields indefinitely. The same trigger also does not update bookingUserName, bookingUserEmail, or bookingUserAvatarUrl when userId changes, so those columns can go stale or stay NULL.
